sections.h2: What kind of county is Clay County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Clay County is a family-heavy county of 604.61 square miles of land with 239,593 residents on July 1, 2025, according to Census QuickFacts. Population is up 9.8% from the April 2020 base of 218,249.

Median household income is $87,820 for 2020 to 2024, the highest of the four Florida counties and cities in this series, and the median owner-occupied home value is $312,500. Owner-occupied units make up 75.9% of 94,791 housing units, and median gross rent is $1,551. Households average 2.69 people, and 22.5% of residents are under 18, while 18.8% are 65 or older.

The mean commute is 31.3 minutes, longer than in the other three places on this set of pages, and 61.7% of people aged 16 and over are in the labor force. The county also counts 27,517 veterans. Those figures describe commuting households with mortgages, so escrow accounts handle most tax payments.

sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who values the property in Clay County?
sections.html:
The Clay County Tax Collector bills and collects, and the Clay County Property Appraiser values property and approves exemptions.

The tax collector's page says bills are mailed by November 1, and that if your mortgage company pays the tax, you receive an information-only copy. Taxes are assessed as of January 1 but are normally payable November 1. Under Florida Statute 197.122, the page says, every owner has a duty to know the amount due and pay before delinquency, so a missing bill does not excuse a late payment.

  • Property appraiser: value, homestead, portability and other exemptions, filed by March 1.
  • Tax collector: payment, installment and partial payment plans, certificate sales.
  • Clerk of the circuit court: records the deed and collects documentary stamp tax.

sections.h2: What are the Clay County discounts and due dates?
sections.html:
The discount is 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February, with no discount in March and delinquency on April 1.

The collector accepts all payment methods. It adds a 2.50% fee to credit card payments and no fee to online e-checks.

sections.h2: How do Clay County installment and partial payment plans work?
sections.html:
Installments need an application by April 30 and estimated taxes above $100, and the first payment is due June 30.

The first installment carries a 6% discount, with no discount if paid in July, and failing to make it by July 31 cancels the plan. The second, due September 30, carries 4.5%. The third, due December 31, carries 3%, and the fourth, due March 31, carries none. The first two installments are based on the prior year's tax notice, while the last two reflect changes in ownership, value or exemptions.

Partial payments are a separate option under Florida Statute 197.374. The owner submits a Partial Payment Plan application with the first payment or in person, and payments can begin November 1. Online payment is not accepted for this plan. Early payment discounts are forfeited, so the full March amount is due, and any balance left on April 1 is delinquent and goes into the June certificate sale.

sections.h2: What happens when Clay County taxes are not paid?
sections.html:
A 3% penalty is added on April 1, additional fees follow on May 1, and a tax certificate sale takes place on or before June 1.

State law then lets the certificate holder apply for a tax deed after two years have passed since April 1 of the year of issuance, with an application fee of $75. The clerk holds the public auction, and the winning bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater. An owner can pay the taxes before the deed issues and stop the sale.

If no one bids, the land goes on the list of lands available for taxes. Ask the Clay County Tax Collector for a payoff amount before you list a home that carries unpaid tax, since fees grow as the process advances.

sections.h2: How do homestead and Save Our Homes cap work in Clay County?
sections.html:
File Form DR-501 with the Clay County Property Appraiser by March 1, with the home as your permanent residence on January 1.

The exemption is up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 covering all taxes and the added $25,000 covering only non-school taxes on value over $50,000. After the first year, yearly growth in assessed value is capped at the lower of 3 percent or CPI, and the Department of Revenue's chart shows a 2.9 percent cap for 2025 and 2.7 percent for 2026. Portability allows a move to a new Florida homestead within three years, with Form DR-501T filed alongside.

Non-homestead property has a separate 10 percent annual limit on assessed value growth. That matters for a rental or second home in Clay County, because its value for tax purposes can still climb every year.

sections.h2: How is the tax settled when you sell a Clay County home?
sections.html:
The closing agent prorates the year's tax, pays any amount due from your proceeds and records the deed with the clerk.

Documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in all counties except Miami-Dade, and the Department of Revenue says all parties to the document are liable no matter who agrees to pay. The tax collector's 2025 note about partial payments applies only to that year, so confirm which tax year your payoff covers.

Because Clay County has a high owner-occupancy rate and many mortgaged homes, many sellers have escrow accounts. Ask your lender for an escrow refund timeline, and ask the tax collector whether the current bill is already paid.

faqs.q: What are the Clay County property tax discounts?
faqs.a: They are 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February. March has no discount, and April 1 is delinquency with a 3% penalty.

faqs.q: When is the Clay County installment application due?
faqs.a: By April 30. Estimated taxes must be above $100, and the first payment is due June 30 for the 6% discount.

faqs.q: Does Clay County charge a fee to pay by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax collector's page states a 2.50% fee on credit card payments, and online e-check payments carry no fee.

faqs.q: When is the Clay County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: On or before June 1, covering the prior year's delinquent real estate taxes. Additional fees apply as of May 1.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for homestead in Clay County?
faqs.a: Apply with the Clay County Property Appraiser by March 1 using Form DR-501. The appraiser decides eligibility, and the tax collector only bills.
